assessment: This is a valuable paper with convincing data. The work presents the first structure of Methanopyrus kandleri Topoisomerase V bound to DNA, revealing two important features of the enzyme's mechanism. The first is that the active site toggles between opened, DNA-accessible state to a closed state where the active site cleft is blocked and inaccessible to nucleic acid. The second is a striking array of helix-hairpin-helix motifs that wrap the duplex DNA. The findings will be of interest to researchers working on understanding structure/function relationships of nucleic acid enzymes, particularly in the topoisomerase and DNA repair fields.
